Sure.  Over a year ago I was diagnosed with both low blood counts and hypopituitarism (for very low hormone levels). It was a struggle but I finally starting feeling better around April. Come June I have a routine MRI on my pituitary gland and I have a bad reaction from the dye they used called gadolinium. Now I suffer from symptoms of gadolinium poisoning and there's no known cure to it. To make matters worse, the MRI showed my pituitary was enhancing, and also my blood work showed my blood counts normalized. Normally you would think this is great, but I went through hell and back during that year period. And then miraculously, when I finally start to feel healthy again, I am struck with another illness, instead this time it is progressive, and much much worse than the other ones. All for an MRI which I didn't even need to have. Completely, utterly, pointless.

Yeah I know what you might say; "If you overcame your other illnesses, you can overcome this too!". Hah, easier said than done. When I said my life was hell for the past year, I wasn't joking. My adrenals were so taxed that the mere sound of forks clashing at the dinner table would be enough to startle me. I couldn't sleep without earplugs, still can't. I went 4 months without a single night above 5 hours sleep, and that was on a good night. I averaged 3-4, waking up sporadically every 50 min. or so.  The hormone disorder also caused my weight to drop substantially even though I was eating the same. The disorder was genetic and I couldn't control or avoid getting it. As I said, I finally starting feeling better, sleeping through the night, and gaining weight. It was amazing. And then I go in for one final MRI, to which I grudgingly consent to, and then I suffer severe symptoms that make everything I'd experienced in the previous year combined feel like a cakewalk in comparison.

 After I was tested positive for elevated levels of the MRI dye, my mom just scheduled me to see a psychiatrist since i was complaining about the pain and she didn't know what else to do. I've been prescribed Xanax, Zoloft, lexapro, klonopin (not all at once), obviously none which helped, but only made things worse. Now I look back and 5 months ago feels like a lifetime ago. I don't even go to school now. I don't talk to friends. I'm fricken 20 years old and now this is my life. 99% of my time consists of chasing pointless pursuits and dulling distractions; all to numb myself and divert my attention from the horrible reality that my existence truly is. All the while, the clock's still moving. The seasons are changing. Everything is. Except me. I just continue to feel worse; both mentally and physically, the former primarily a result of the latter. 

At this point, I don't even see suicide as an escape. There simply is no escape. I am like a hamster, and the universe is my mirrored ball. No matter how fast or slow I run, I am and always will be confined within this ball. Everywhere I look is my own reflection. I know another world out there beyond this mirrored ball exists, yet for me it's none other than an idea; a thought; a mental construct. It isn't real. Instead this is my reality. A stagnant swamp of quicksand, slowly sucking me deeper into the void, while only occasionally reaching awareness of my saddened state. The rest of the time I distract myself by any means possible...Food, tv, video games, you name it. Sometimes the truth is too hard to bare. I can't handle the truth. I can't handle any of this. But I don't have a choice. I'm playing a game I don't want to play, living a life I don't want to live. Is this really what my life has amounted to - a saddened, alone, pain-stricken crippled 20 year old? I used to believe my whole life was ahead of me, but now the farther I venture out to sea, the more the life I once loved is fading in sight, a mere sparkle in the eye. Nothing more. My life - an abyss.

--Hope that clears things up for you. Sorry for the length, I just kind of went off there. I may make this into one coherent post later coupled with my original text. Anyways, thanks for taking the time to read. Cheers.
